answer_1.quote: Task-specific Natural Language Generation (NLG) aims to generate texts that satisfy desired attributes of target tasks, such as text style transfer and task-specific data augmentation.
answer_1.outputs: generated texts for new tasks in zero-shot and few-shot settings, including style-transferred sentences and augmented examples for classification

answer_2.quote: We use the widely adopted metric ACC avg in continual learning, which measures the performance by averaging the accuracies of the classifier on test sets of all seen tasks... In addition, to measure the diversity of generated examples, we calculate the average similarity scores between all pairs of examples within each label, i.e. 1 |Y| i,j sim(x i , x j )1[arg max p(y|x i ) == arg max p(y|x j )], where we use BLEU and word mover distance (WMD) as the similarity functions.
